title: Why buy a turnkey business: skipping research, setup and customer acquisition
summary: Ross Jenkins argues that buying an existing turnkey business beats starting from scratch because you inherit market research, a proven model, a loyal customer base and seller support. It is a generic, listicle-style case for acquisition over startup, with a closing reminder to do due diligence and consult experts before signing.

principles.text: Buying an existing business lets you reuse prior market research and inventory data instead of researching from zero.
principles.quote: Since it is not new to the market and has been at the same location for a while, you have insight into the customers.

principles.text: A proven, replicable model removes guesswork about strategy and profit maximization for new owners.
principles.quote: Turnkey businesses offer a setup that eliminates the guesswork common with new entrepreneurs who are unsure of which strategy to use to maximize profit.

principles.text: Winning customers from competitors is the hardest part of business and often costs heavy discounts; an established base avoids that.
principles.quote: The hardest part about running a business is getting people to switch from a competitor’s product to yours.

principles.text: Existing customers cut the marketing spend and promotional offers a from-scratch startup needs to attract buyers.
principles.quote: Starting a business from scratch entails a lot of marketing costs and offers to attract new customers.

principles.text: Seller support (tech, marketing, training, operations) raises your odds of success after a purchase.
principles.quote: By partnering with a supportive business franchisor, you have better chances of driving your business in the right direction and increasing your chances of success.

principles.text: Do thorough due diligence before buying: research, talk to current owners, and consult experts.
principles.quote: before settling for any turnkey business you come across, remember to conduct thorough research and schedule a consultation with the current business owners before signing a contract.
